Lookahead: zero-width assertion. Checks whether a pattern matches at the current position, consumes no characters → match continues from the same spot, and the looked-at text isn't part of the result.

`(?=...)` positive: must match ahead. `(?!...)` negative: must not.

```
\d+(?= USD)     "100 USD" → matches "100", not " USD"
\d+(?! USD)     "100 EUR" → matches "100"
^(?=.*\d)(?=.*[a-z]).{8,}$    multiple lookaheads at same position = AND conditions
```

Gotcha: negative lookahead plus backtracking gives surprises. `\d+(?! USD)` on "100 USD" matches "10", because the engine backs off one digit and "0 USD" isn't " USD". Fix: `\d+\b(?! USD)` or possessive/atomic `\d++(?! USD)`.

Supported in nearly all engines (PCRE, JS, Python, Java, .NET); not in RE2/Go `regexp` or POSIX `grep -E`.
